clue.text: PM once ditching head of state in Barnet

indicators.note: ditching means throwing out, so the head of state is dropped from the former prime minister

parts.note: Margaret Thatcher was UK prime minister from 1979 to 1990
ER, Elizabeth Regina, the Queen as head of state

explanation.surface: A former prime minister drops in on a north London borough minus some dignitary.
explanation.walkthrough: Barnet is a London borough, but here it is Cockney rhyming slang: Barnet Fair = hair. 'ditching' removes ER (the Queen) from the end of the PM's surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal British words for a head of hair, one rhyming slang and the other a roofing image.

clue.text: Bully's horrible nature, one admitted?

definitions.note: the definition is a possessive, belonging to a bull, matching the adjective

indicators.note: admitted means let in, so the one goes inside
horrible suggests something mangled, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Is a bully's nature horrible, a question of character?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bully' is a bull here; 'horrible' rearranges NATURE around I.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means of or like a bull, from the Latin word taurus.

clue.text: Addle-pated or highly able?

indicators.note: addle means to confuse or scramble, so the following word is rearranged

explanation.surface: Is someone muddled, or really clever?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Addle-pated' is one word for muddled, but splits into an anagram signal and its fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym for skilled and proficient, highly expert.

clue.text: Star's sleeveless garment lifted completely

definitions.note: the definition is the star; the 's stands for is

parts.note: a cape is a sleeveless cloak

indicators.note: lifted means raised, which in a down clue reads the word upwards

parts.note: all can mean completely, as in all gone

explanation.surface: A celebrity's cloak has been stolen outright.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lifted' suggests theft, but it turns ALL upward in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the brightest star in the constellation Auriga.

clue.text: Retiring soldiers work with country prone to infiltration

indicators.note: retiring means drawing back, so the soldiers and the work are read backwards together

parts.note: OR, other ranks, the ordinary soldiers
OP is short for opus, a musical work
US, the United States

explanation.surface: Troops withdraw while a nation's defences are easily breached.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retiring' acts on both the soldiers and the work together, not on the soldiers alone; OR for other ranks is a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: Something with many tiny holes lets liquid or air seep through, so it is easily permeated.

clue.text: Cost of no longer popular piece of music

parts.note: something out of fashion is out
a lay is a song or ballad

explanation.surface: The price paid for a song that has fallen from favour.
explanation.definitionFit: Money spent on something is its expenditure or cost.

clue.text: After a few balls, berobed queen's running wild

indicators.note: after means following, so the robed queen comes after the balls

parts.note: an over in cricket is a set of six balls
R, the queen, wearing a gown: GOWN with R inside

explanation.surface: After a few dances, the gowned queen is dancing wildly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'balls' are cricket deliveries, not dances; an over is six of them. 'berobed' puts R (Regina, queen) inside GOWN.
explanation.definitionFit: A garden left untended has plants growing wildly out of control.

clue.text: Penny wearing Eve's top?

indicators.note: wearing means having on, so the sinner surrounds the penny

parts.note: Eve, who ate the forbidden fruit, is a sinner; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: A coin sits inside Eve's shirt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top' is not a garment but a spinning toy.
explanation.definitionFit: A spinning top is one kind of toy that whirls, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Killer arrested by lawman, getting sudden comedown

indicators.note: arrested by means held by, so the lawman surrounds the killer

parts.note: a fed is a US federal agent
an orca or orc is a killer whale
landing a job means getting it

explanation.surface: A murderer is caught by an agent and suffers a sharp fall.
explanation.definitionFit: An emergency touchdown by an aircraft forced to come down abruptly.

clue.text: Drug that doesn't work for man?

parts.note: a dud is something that fails to function
E is ecstasy, the drug

explanation.surface: A useless pill passed off as something else.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces appear in the clue in reverse order: the drug comes first in the clue but last in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: In American slang the word is a casual form of address for a fellow, a guy.

clue.text: Medical substitute aces academic assignment

parts.note: aces are experts, professionals or pros
a thesis is a long piece of academic writing

explanation.surface: Top students hand in excellent work on a medical topic.
explanation.definitionFit: An artificial limb or similar device replaces a missing body part.

clue.text: Information on length for supporting beam

indicators.note: in an across clue one thing on another sits after it, so the information follows the length

parts.note: intel is informal for intelligence or information

explanation.surface: Data about the span needed for a structural support.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the horizontal beam over a door or window that carries the weight above.

clue.text: What makes daughter a palace attraction?

parts.note: rearranging the letters of the two final words of the answer gives the word daughter

explanation.surface: A puzzle question: what turns a girl into a royal tourist draw?
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: the answer read as wordplay, 'changing' as an anagram signal acting on its last two words, produces DAUGHTER.
explanation.definitionFit: The ceremonial handover of sentries at Buckingham Palace draws large crowds of tourists.

clue.text: American rockers make time for artist

parts.note: R.E.M. are an American rock band
a make is a brand of product

explanation.surface: A US rock group takes time off to become a painter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make' is a noun here, as in a make of car, not a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dutch Golden Age master is one of the most famous painters, an example of an artist.

clue.text: Missing king to get dubbed ignorant

indicators.note: missing means lacking, so the king is removed

parts.note: being dubbed is being knighted
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: Without the monarch present, one cannot be dubbed.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally overtaken by night, figuratively unenlightened or in intellectual darkness.

clue.text: Coat's wrapped round figure

indicators.note: wrapped means enclosed, so the coat goes round the circle shape

parts.note: an animal's coat is its fur; the 's stands for is
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A fur coat is draped around someone's body shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'figure' looks like the body the coat wraps, but it is a number.
explanation.definitionFit: A figure is a numeral, and this is one of the digits.

clue.text: Billionaire's acquired island

indicators.note: acquired means held or owned, so the island sits within the word

explanation.surface: A tycoon has bought himself an island.
explanation.definitionFit: The small Hebridean isle off western Scotland is famous for its abbey.

clue.text: People wearing religious clothing

definitions.note: to people a place is to populate it, a verb

parts.note: in can mean wearing, as in in uniform
a habit is a monk's or nun's robe

explanation.surface: Folk dressed in monastic robes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'People' is a verb here, to populate.
explanation.definitionFit: To populate a place is to live there and occupy it.

clue.text: A feature film's about manual worker

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the film goes around the other pieces

parts.note: a mist is a thin film or haze; the 's stands for is
the chin is a facial feature

explanation.surface: A feature film is about a factory hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'feature film' reads as one phrase but splits: 'feature' is a part of the face and 'film' a haze.
explanation.definitionFit: This worker operates machines by hand, a sewing machinist being a common example.

clue.text: High tea during hard period for concubine

indicators.note: during means within, so the jumbled drink goes inside

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard on pencils
an era is a period of time

indicators.note: high suggests intoxicated, so the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: Taking an evening meal during tough times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High tea' reads as an early evening meal, but 'High' (as in intoxicated) is what scrambles the drink, giving ETA.
explanation.definitionFit: In ancient Greece this was a courtesan or mistress, a kept woman.

clue.text: Fifty Shades-type behaviour an unwelcome sight in the bedroom

parts.note: Fifty Shades of Grey features S and M, sadomasochism

explanation.surface: Kinky goings-on, unwanted in the bedroom.
explanation.walkthrough: The bedroom sight is not sexual: it is the folk figure who sprinkles sand to bring sleep, unwelcome to a child who wants to stay up.
explanation.definitionFit: The bringer of sleep is a figure children dread at bedtime.

clue.text: Lascivious, heartless church bigwig

indicators.note: heartless means losing the middle, so the central letters are removed

parts.note: a cardinal is a senior Catholic churchman

explanation.surface: A senior clergyman who is lustful and cruel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' removes DI, the middle two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym meaning of the flesh, sensual and lustful.

clue.text: See 12
Works out riddle, having succeeded finally

indicators.note: finally means at the end, so the succeeded letter goes last

parts.note: to riddle is to sift through a sieve, to strain
S is the abbreviation for succeeded in genealogies

explanation.surface: Someone cracks a puzzle, managing it in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'riddle' looks like a puzzle but is a coarse sieve; the S moves from the front to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To work out at the gym is to exercise, to get in shape.

clue.text: Signal recalling marines

parts.note: à la means in the style of, so recalling
RM is the Royal Marines

explanation.surface: A call to the troops to return.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalling' suggests turning back, but no reversal: it is the French à la, in the manner of.
explanation.definitionFit: A warning sound or bell is a signal of danger.

clue.text: Doing without six-pack, having drunk 9 etc

parts.note: a six-pack is toned abdominal muscles, abs

indicators.note: drunk means disordered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the number nine written as a word

explanation.surface: Giving up beer while holding a six-pack of something.
explanation.walkthrough: '9' is not a cross-reference here but the word NINE, which with ETC is mixed up to give TINENCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Refraining from something, especially alcohol, means going without it.

clue.text: Rounds with ham, more sandwiches

indicators.note: sandwiches means holds between, so the answer lies across the words

explanation.surface: A round of sandwiches filled with ham, and seconds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rounds' suggests rounds of sandwiches, but they are bullets.
explanation.definitionFit: Ammunition comes as rounds, each round a single cartridge or shell.

clue.text: Slightly tight clothing for damsel in order to go around

indicators.note: to go around means encircling, so the neat word surrounds the girl's outside letters

parts.note: something tidy is in order

indicators.note: clothing is the outer covering, so take the edges of the word damsel

explanation.surface: A tight dress makes a young woman look neat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tight' means drunk, not snug.
explanation.definitionFit: British informal for a little drunk, mildly tipsy.

clue.text: Good God! This is a bit of a pig

parts.note: Ammon was the chief god of ancient Egypt

explanation.surface: An exclamation of surprise at seeing part of a pig.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Good God!' reads as an oath, but it is two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: It is cured meat from the hind leg of a pig, so a piece of the animal.
